What is the minimal value of d that guarantees positive stability of A? Does the minimal stability-guaranteeing value of d depend on the matrix order n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let A be a real n×n P-matrix, i.e. a matrix all of whose principal minors are positive. For index sets α, β ⊆ {1,…,n} with #α = #β, let A[α,β] denote the minor of A with row index set α and column index set β, and define the dispersal of A[α,β] to be #α − #(α∩β). A is called positively stable if every eigenvalue of A has positive real part.

For a nonnegative integer d, say that A satisfies the dispersal-d sign-symmetry condition if
   A[α,β] · A[β,α] ≥ 0
for every pair (α,β) with #α = #β and dispersal at most d. It is known that d = 1 is not sufficient to force positive stability of every n×n P-matrix satisfying the condition (a counterexample exists), while d = n is sufficient (Carlson's theorem on sign-symmetric P-matrices).

Determine the minimal value d = d(n) such that every n×n P-matrix satisfying the dispersal-d sign-symmetry condition is positively stable. In particular, decide whether this minimal value depends on the order n.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is one of the explicitly stated open problems on GKK τ-matrices. The literature shows that the conjecture d=1 suffices was disproved by counterexamples (unstable GKK τ-matrices), and d=n suffices by Carlson's theorem, but no determination of the minimal sufficient dispersal threshold (or its dependence on n) appears in subsequent work; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on GKK τ-matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems concerning stability of GKK τ-matrices including the dispersal threshold question.
status_evidence.claim: The dispersal-threshold question is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Theorems and counterexamples on structured matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples showing not all GKK τ-matrices are stable; classical conjectures disproved.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature provides counterexamples but does not resolve the minimal dispersal threshold.
